terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, transitive; ab + abl.
evidence: Cic. Arch. 4: nōn modo nōn sēgregandum ā numerō cīvium (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From grex: to take out of the flock, and so to set anyone or anything apart from the rest (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, transitive; ab + abl.
evidence: Cic. Cat. 1.32: mūrō dēnique sēcernantur ā nōbīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To part one thing from another, as bad olives from good (Columella) or the conspirators from the city.
Rare but classical (Lewis & Short): to shut up in a place of its own, as Varro the ewes about to lamb. An isolated place is sōlitārius or dēvius.

phrases.latin: inter capellās agnō bālantī canis: stulte, inquit, errās; nōn est hīc māter tua; ovēsque sēgregātās ostendit procul
phrases.english: to a lamb bleating among the she-goats a dog said: “Silly, you’re wrong; your mother isn’t here,” and pointed to the sheep, kept apart some way off

phrases.latin: Ovem aegram ā cēterīs sēgregā, nē morbus serpat.
phrases.english: Keep the sick sheep away from the others, so the illness doesn’t spread.

sources: Lewis & Short: segrego · Lewis & Short: secerno · Lewis & Short: secludo
